# Checkpoint 04 audit addendum

## New mathematical results

**F.3.13** constructs the actual affine finite-presentation automorphism group of a rigid exact integral tensor category admissibly generated by one object. Its construction works on every coefficient algebra, including algebras with torsion or nilpotents. Subobjects and quotients use split sequences of finite projective modules; both the universal automorphism and its inverse preserve the chosen presentations. Naturality and tensor equations then define the complete functor inside a general linear group. The finiteness argument of F.3.12 applies to these precisely specified stages over S-integers. The actual historical `M_alpha` has not yet been identified with this category, so I.M09.01 remains OPEN. The newly obtained original cote15 opening directly uses `T_alpha` without supplying that missing definition.

**F.3.14** constructs a finite birational morphism from every smooth integral projective d-fold over a characteristic-zero field to an integral hypersurface in projective (d+1)-space. The source is exactly the normalization: this is proved by the affine integral-closure argument. The sections and the primitive element defining the morphism are specified. The nodal cubic gives a fully computed boundary to an ordinary-cohomology reading: its normalization is P1, and the two-branch difference map produces a one-dimensional kernel in degree one. The source and target of every displayed cohomology map are retained. This result supplies a modern exact construction, but does not identify execution of the particular historical standard-conjecture proposal in cote14. I.M05.01 and II.MB08.01 remain DOCUMENTARY-GAP.

Root independently checked the full proofs of F.3.13 and F.3.14 and passed them. A new dedicated integer-polynomial certificate for F.3.14 verifies the cubic equation after substitution, the two projective chart assertions proving no common zero, the rational inverse, and the two node preimages. No unrelated certificate was rerun.

## New historical result

**G.2.3**, in `sections/G_history_sources.tex`, records the newly obtained original May1966 letter to Tate. The original heading and final numbered p30 were inspected visually. The official Montpellier inventory independently names the May1966 letter; CSG catalogues it as unpublished. The text asks for the generic-fibre Tate module from Dieudonne and lifted-filtration data, initially under the ordinary-type reduction qualification of section3.1, then asks about more general groups.

The degree-one comparison map is written through an ordinary abelian scheme: cohomological H1_et is the dual of the covariant rational Tate module; Dcris identifies the former with H1_cris and its lifted Hodge filtration; the period-ring intersection reconstructs the rational Galois representation. The covariant Dieudonne dictionary retains the (-1) twist, sigma-semilinearity, F and V, and the annihilator filtration. Integral Tate lattices still use the integral data of Part B. Root independently checked these maps.

This establishes a dated written antecedent to the Nice1970 formulation. It does not date the individual leaf18:5. That leaf has no visible date or dated reused typescript; the adjacent reused sheet has not been established to be its physical verso. Dossier-level1969–1972 dating is not promoted to an individual terminus post quem. No absolute earliest formulation is claimed. Quotations from the newly retrieved letter total22 words in the manuscript.

## Remaining original-source gates

Additional exact-title and content searches in the connected Library did not retrieve the originals of Fontaine–Messing1987, Faltings1989, Tsuji1999, Sen1973, or Kisin2006. Their previously recorded attempts and explicitly named primary substitutes remain unchanged. Derivative returns were not promoted to original sources.

The Kleiman1968 primary text was opened through the cached full article; its live URL now returns404. Its explicit modern A/B/C/D/I dictionary does not identify the separate unnamed B,D entries in the1967 Coates letter. Those precise naming obligations remain documentary gaps.

The EGA V Blass translation was opened at Proposition14.5 and Corollary14.6, printed p58, as an exact projection-source lead. The complete original French171-page PDF was then obtained (16,097,021 bytes), and original p89 Proposition14.5/Corollary14.6 was visually checked at180dpi, together with the preceding p88. The corrected original explicitly states the birational morphism onto a hypersurface and notes that it need not be an immersion. Its preceding differential-property proof is left to Dieudonne. F3.14 therefore retains the independent proof, while adding the exact original citation. The separate cote14 historical execution remains unlocated.
